title: AI papers in the arXiv announcement batch of 2026-10-23
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This is a curated inferred ordering based on sparse secondary coverage and demonstrated relevance; citation evidence is limited for newly announced papers, so it is not a measured popularity ranking.

sections.title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
sections.abstract: The authors introduce a benchmark of 300 matched safe/unsafe task pairs across six domains to test whether tool-using agents act safely when critical facts are omitted and whether they retrieve and use those facts appropriately.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper claims EpiSEM-Bench separates unsafe execution, safety boundaries, and evidence recovery; its ten-model study finds that robustness to omissions does not by itself imply useful recovery.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence is from a bounded benchmark (300 task pairs, six domains, ten model configurations, and a fixed evaluation protocol); transfer to other tools, tasks, and deployments remains to be established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Secondary coverage of the missing-evidence safety failure mode, plus relevance of the matched-world protocol and ten-model evaluation; these are relevance signals, not readership statistics.

sections.title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
sections.abstract: The authors propose selecting partial reasoning traces by directly optimizing the probability that at least one retained trace finishes correctly, balancing quality and diversity to reduce the cost of test-time scaling.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors’ PKTP method models correlated rollout outcomes, uses a second-order submodular approximation to pass@$k$, and greedily produces nested candidate sets; experiments report improvements over quality-only and diversity-only pruning baselines.
sections.unique_caveat: The approach depends on a latent-Gaussian model of correlated rollout success and on information in partial-trace representations; the authors identify stronger representations as a direct future-work need.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A technical summary listing and comparisons on eight open-weight reasoning models, with largest gains at moderate retained-pool sizes; relevance, not demonstrated broad popularity.

sections.title: Reliable AI-Assisted Decisions via Selective Auditing
sections.abstract: This paper formulates online AI decision review as constrained optimization and presents auditing policies intended to limit the share of AI errors that escape expert review while minimizing how often review is needed.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors derive online error-control methods, including one they characterize as asymptotically optimally efficient for adversarial and i.i.d. streams, and report lower auditing effort than baselines on three task types.
sections.unique_caveat: The discussion assumes auditors are correct and audits have equal cost; noisy auditors and heterogeneous audit costs are left for future work. The appendix cautions that a capped variant can weaken error control when errors are rare.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The work is surfaced in Berkeley-hosted and BU CISE institutional pages; its error-control framing and evaluations across three task types establish relevance, not independent popularity.

sections.title: RIDAR: Safeguarding Research Integrity in Autonomous Research Agents via Automated Detection and Runtime Intervention
sections.abstract: RIDAR combines a taxonomy of research-integrity violations, post-hoc trajectory detection, and runtime intervention; the authors report 85.2% F1 on a 60-trajectory annotated benchmark and 36.8% fewer violations remaining at task completion in their runtime evaluation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim a full-lifecycle taxonomy and paired post-hoc/runtime monitoring framework, reporting 3,964 detected violations across 300 trajectories and a reduction in remaining violations after runtime intervention.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported detection and intervention results are tied to the paper’s expert-labeled set and collected trajectories; performance on other agent architectures and independently generated research workflows is not established here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A Hugging Face Papers listing, a secondary research digest, and the authors’ repository surfaced; the taxonomy and evaluation results make it relevant to research-agent reliability.

sections.title: Adaptive Skill Granularity for Coding Agents: Runtime Routing and Macro-to-Micro Recovery
sections.abstract: The authors treat skill granularity as a runtime control decision, routing coding agents among primitive actions, macro skills, and macro-to-micro recovery when a macro fails.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that runtime routing and explicit macro-to-micro recovery improve robustness over fixed-granularity execution in their deterministic coding-agent protocol, while selective recovery avoids some unnecessary costs.
sections.unique_caveat: The evaluation uses a small set of mixed coding tasks and controlled injected failures, with a few hand-written macros; the authors explicitly call for broader tasks, repositories, failure modes, and models.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Secondary coverage in Nowness AI and AI Pulse plus verifier-defined success and controlled recovery experiments; the small pilot limits broader trend claims.
